title: MCP server drops every message when a persistent client batches them into one read — real handshake never completes
evidence: main.m:13 reads with `[input availableData]` and parses each raw read as exactly ONE object via `NSJSONSerialization JSONObjectWithData:options:0` (options:0 rejects a buffer holding more than one top-level JSON value). A persistent stdio MCP client sends newline-delimited messages that the OS pipe delivers batched in a single read (initialize + notifications/initialized + tools/list), so the multi-object buffer parses to nil and `if(!request)continue;` silently drops all of them. Reproduced against the bundled binary: single `initialize` → valid reply; batched init+initialized+tools/list in one write → 0 replies; the SAME three messages delivered with 0.4s gaps (separate reads) → 3 replies. Confirmed by _runtime.json ('did not complete the MCP handshake: no reply to tools/list within 30s') and _factual.json (score 0.0). The run's own tests/run_tests.sh:3 masks the bug because `run()` spawns a fresh process per single message.
suggestion: Buffer stdin and frame on newlines (split the accumulated NSData on '\n' and decode each complete line as its own JSON object), rather than assuming one `availableData` read == one message.
